title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 12

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the audit session begin?
tasks.audioText: The quality auditor will explain evidence sampling on Monday at nine thirty. Students should meet in the quality office and bring the audit checklist. The session will compare document samples, interview notes and process observations. The auditor will explain why a finding must refer to a requirement and identify the evidence that supports it.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which audit tool should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The quality auditor will explain evidence sampling on Monday at nine thirty. Students should meet in the quality office and bring the audit checklist. The session will compare document samples, interview notes and process observations. The auditor will explain why a finding must refer to a requirement and identify the evidence that supports it.
options: The sampling plan and audit report
The process map and action log
The quality manual and non-conformance form

tasks.prompt: An audit finding should be linked to a defined requirement. The auditor records the evidence observed, identifies the relevant document or process and explains how the evidence relates to the requirement. A finding should not be based only on an opinion. If the evidence is incomplete, the auditor may request additional information before reaching a conclusion. Reading 1. What should an audit finding be linked to?
What should happen if the evidence is incomplete?
options: The finding should be closed as compliant
The requirement should be changed to match the evidence
The previous audit result should be accepted without review
Additional information should be requested before reaching a conclusion

tasks.prompt: The audit finding ___ to a defined requirement.
Choose TWO forms of evidence that may support an audit finding.
Information that can be examined to support an audit finding is objective ___.
A finding is based on an opinion but has no evidence reference. What should you ask?
options: Could we identify the requirement and the evidence that supports this finding?
The evidence reference can be removed.
I will approve it without checking.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of quality audit evidence in a logical order.
options: Compare the evidence with the requirement
Record a finding that is supported by evidence
correctOrder: Compare the evidence with the requirement
Record a finding that is supported by evidence

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words explaining how an audit finding should connect a requirement with objective evidence.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Requirement — 2: identifies the applicable requirement or criterion; 1: partial; 0: absent. (2) Objective evidence — 2: describes specific, verifiable evidence and its source; 1: partial; 0: absent. (3) Finding statement — 2: clearly links the evidence to the requirement and avoids unsupported conclusions; 1: partial; 0: no clear link or speculative. (4) English — 2: concise audit language and accurate quality vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
